quarterly_data.signal: H1 2026: the commercial model has moved from spot orders to long-term agreements, which management calls the cornerstone of the new strategy. CEO Jutta Bechwati: "The major difference here is really that we've moved completely from a spot order approach to long-term agreements... it gives us visibility on the utilization of our assets. It gives us visibility on how to better manage really any kind of supply into the sites and really enables us to plan for capacity expansion ahead of time." More LTAs are in the pipeline: "there is quite a bit in the pipeline right now that we are working on", though "some of these agreements will come with announcements, others will not".

H1 2026: the commercial milestones signed in the 133 days since the strategic review concluded and MACOM invested - "As well as the multi-year agreements with MACOM, we've also signed a multi-year Indium Phosphide agreement with Tower Semiconductor, a $14 million production order with an AI and data center customer. Just last week, we announced a purchase agreement with Quintessence for Quantum Dot Laser epitaxy." Management frames quantum dot lasers as "the next wave of innovation for data center applications".
quarterly_data.figure: $14 million production order from an unnamed AI and data center customer; multi-year Indium Phosphide agreement with Tower Semiconductor; Quintessence quantum dot laser epitaxy purchase agreement

quarterly_data.signal: H1 2026: first-half revenue GBP 64.6 million, up 43% year-on-year. Wireless GBP 26 million, up 40%, "reflecting market share gains and increased sales of wireless mobile connectivity solutions across newly qualified customer platforms". Photonics GBP 38.5 million, up 45%, "driven by funding releases for certain U.S. military and defense programs, and continued growth in AI and data center-related markets". Growth was not only year-on-year but half-on-half, and Photonics is now the larger of the two reported segments.
quarterly_data.figure: Revenue GBP 64.6 million (+43% YoY); Wireless GBP 26 million (+40%); Photonics GBP 38.5 million (+45%); adjusted EBITDA GBP 6 million

quarterly_data.signal: H1 2026: the margin improvement is operational, not price-led - "driven by better utilization of our manufacturing capacity alongside a more favorable product mix, as Photonics made up a greater proportion of sales", plus "yield improvements and activities around really truly reestablishing operational excellence in all of our areas" built over the last 18 months. Management stresses the revenue expansion was delivered on the existing asset base: "we are able to achieve the revenue expansion, really, with the existing assets". Yields and production outputs improved across all sites, and a new COO (Matt Geen) was appointed to run operational oversight.
quarterly_data.figure: adjusted EBITDA GBP 6 million; revenue expansion delivered on existing assets

quarterly_data.signal: H1 2026: the balance-sheet transformation is complete and now funds the expansion - "We have gone from being a heavily leveraged business at the year-end to now being completely free of bank debt with a cash position of GBP 41.6 million." Adjusted net cash was GBP 30.2 million after a GBP 4 million working-capital outflow. Management describes a "fully funded balance sheet" and has announced an intention to apply for a LSE main market listing, targeting admission in first half 2027.
quarterly_data.figure: cash GBP 41.6 million; adjusted net cash GBP 30.2 million; zero bank debt; GBP 4 million working-capital outflow

quarterly_data.signal: H1 2026: upgraded full-year guidance reiterated - "Following our July trading update, where we've upgraded full-year guidance, we have seen the strong momentum continue into the second half of the year... As a result, we are very confident of reaching our upgraded guidance", with the upside case tied to "the rising demand for optical communications for data center and AI infrastructure, which is underpinned by our recently signed supply agreements". A webcast questioner quoted the going-concern statement's at least 30% growth in both 2026 and 2027; management did not dispute it and said the outlook will only be revised once LTA visibility and the Indium Phosphide substrate bottleneck allow. A strategy reset with new long-term margin, revenue and growth targets, and a new segment reporting structure, is promised for 2027.
quarterly_data.figure: upgraded FY2026 guidance reiterated; going-concern statement cites at least 30% growth in both 2026 and 2027 (quoted by a webcast questioner, not disputed by management)

quarterly_data.signal: H1 2026: Indium Phosphide substrate supply and rare earth bottlenecks are the gating risks, and the second-half outlook already reflects them - "there is substrate supply concerns, as well as rare earth bottlenecks that are highlighted in each of the calls that you are seeing in the industry... the second half outlook already reflects these risks... not over-committing to a number that we will not be able to hit". On InP specifically: "Indium Phosphide substrates are becoming some of the bottlenecks around significant volume increases. Therefore, we are working closely with everybody in the industry and with all partners to ensure that we are locking in volume allocations to secure our demand that we are currently seeing with our customers."

H1 2026: the InP substrate diameter mix, from the epiwafer maker's own view - "3-inch is still very dominant. Then it's 4-inch with almost half of the volume driven by 4-inch, and only then comes 6-inch as the fastest-growing sort of diameter, and it's scaling right now." 6-inch maturity and line yields still need to improve and "we are not seeing truly the really demand on 6-inch yet". Management clarified that IQE's tool conversions are material conversions (Gallium Arsenide to Indium Phosphide), which "doesn't necessarily come with a dimension conversion"; IQE can support 3-inch, 4-inch and 6-inch. Tightness across the three diameters is hard to rank because "there is different types of substrates too".
quarterly_data.figure: InP substrate volume mix: 3-inch dominant, 4-inch almost half of volume, 6-inch fastest growing but least mature

quarterly_data.signal: H1 2026: capacity is being added by converting existing tooling in the second half "to increase capacity to meet the strong demand for Indium Phosphide", and every conversion is gated on a signed customer commitment - "we will also not expand capacity without a clear customer commitment and a clear visibility on what value is going to be driven with that expansion" and "we are still not converting tools without customer commitments and secured demand on these tools". Conversion cost is "definitely insignificant compared to the cost of a new reactor"; the real cost is the downtime of the tool. Customer prepayments are "definitely a mechanism for us to fund our growth", following what "some of our players in the same ecosystem" already do. Newport still has "ample clean room space to add capacity" so IQE "can scale up rather quickly compared to others because we already have the infrastructure to house these reactors".

H1 2026: IQE's routes into AI and data center are four distinct epitaxy platforms - "high demand for our Indium Phosphide and Gallium Arsenide optical interconnect technologies", "gallium nitride on silicon MicroLED epitaxy for partners serving hyperscalers for high bandwidth, energy efficient data transfer in AI data centers", and "gallium nitride on silicon power epitaxy, meeting the need for high efficiency power supply units within data center infrastructure". Management stresses the reach is wider than the data center: "we are really playing into all spaces of AI from really the rack to the edge". On pricing, "we are in a much better position really to demand higher pricing, especially for our bespoke solutions", though long-term customer relationships are said to outrank short-term price increases.

H1 2026: the Taiwan site is no longer for sale. The proposed divestment was "driven of the necessity, looking at our balance sheet, and really the need to fund the existing debt structure"; with the balance sheet repaired, "there is no need to sell anything right now... we are not looking into selling anything at the moment, and not in the foreseeable future either". Management now frames the multi-geography footprint as a supply hedge: the inclusion of Taiwan "enables us really to play into geopolitical situations that we can deliver into all existing markets and really offset some of the constraints that others would be seeing".

quarterly_data.signal: H1 2026: GaN power arrived later than IQE expected but is now inflecting, and MicroLED is overtaking it - "from a technology perspective, GaN power has shifted to the right, but we are now seeing really significant pickup on that opportunity. MicroLED as part of also the overall GaN technology application footprint is really gaining more and more momentum on that and really is almost surpassing the GaN power application." The data center pull is specific on both: "gallium nitride on silicon power epitaxy, meeting the need for high efficiency power supply units within data center infrastructure", and "gallium nitride on silicon MicroLED epitaxy for partners serving hyperscalers for high bandwidth, energy efficient data transfer in AI data centers".
quarterly_data.figure: no specific figure (GaN and MicroLED are not separately disclosed; H1 group revenue GBP 64.6 million)

quarterly_data.signal: H1 2026: RF, defense and satcom are a second pillar for the compound-epitaxy business - "new product qualifications and design wins across terrestrials, satellites, including low Earth orbit, and defense radar platforms", plus an expanded gallium antimonide infrared customer base "into new geographies around the world". Management: "we have been a very substantial part of the overall military and defense ecosystem in the U.S. already, especially with our infrared sensing technology based on our gallium antimonide technologies", supplying "the prime companies that are playing in that space". Photonics revenue growth in the half was partly driven by "funding releases for certain U.S. military and defense programs".
